Get started with georgiacivicdata

Source: vignettes/georgiacivicdata.Rmd
georgiacivicdata.Rmd

georgiacivicdata reads the Georgia Civic Data API: cleaned public data about Georgia’s schools and communities. This article walks through the everyday workflow: find a dataset, understand it, get its rows, and cite it.

library(georgiacivicdata)
library(dplyr)

Find data

gcd_search() ranks datasets from plain words, in English or Spanish:

gcd_search("students missing a lot of school", n = 5) |>
  select(rank, name, title, year_min, year_max)
#> ℹ Lookup tables that match: "schools" and "districts". See `gcd_dimension()`.
#> # A tibble: 5 × 5
#>    rank name              title                                year_min year_max
#>   <int> <chr>             <chr>                                   <int>    <int>
#> 1     1 attendance        Student Attendance and Chronic Abse…     2004     2025
#> 2     2 dropout_rate_7_12 Grade 7-12 Dropout Rates                 2011     2025
#> 3     3 dropout_rate_9_12 Grades 9-12 Dropout Rates                2011     2025
#> 4     4 retained_students Retained (Held-Back) K-12 Students       2004     2025
#> 5     5 school_enrollment School Enrollment of Children (ACS)      2020     2024

gcd_datasets() is the whole catalog, one row per dataset. Every argument narrows it on the server:

catalog <- gcd_datasets()
count(catalog, main_topic, kind)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 3
#>   main_topic  kind         n
#>   <chr>       <chr>    <int>
#> 1 census      table       28
#> 2 education   geometry     2
#> 3 education   table       61
#> 4 health      table       62
#> 5 immigration table       23

gcd_datasets(main_topic = "education", level = "districts", year = 2025) |>
  select(name, title)
#> # A tibble: 51 × 2
#>    name                                     title                               
#>    <chr>                                    <chr>                               
#>  1 ccrpi_content_mastery                    CCRPI Content Mastery               
#>  2 ccrpi_graduation_rate                    High School Graduation Rates        
#>  3 ccrpi_progress                           CCRPI Progress                      
#>  4 ccrpi_readiness                          CCRPI Readiness                     
#>  5 ccrpi_scoring_by_component               CCRPI Scores and Components         
#>  6 enrollment_by_grade                      Enrollment by Grade Level (Fall and…
#>  7 enrollment_march_gender_race_ethnicity   March Enrollment by Race and Gender 
#>  8 enrollment_october_disability            Special Education Enrollment by Dis…
#>  9 enrollment_october_gender_race_ethnicity October Enrollment by Race and Gend…
#> 10 free_reduced_lunch                       Free and Reduced-Price Lunch Eligib…
#> # ℹ 41 more rows

Understand a dataset

gcd_describe() prints what a dataset holds, where it comes from, its years and detail levels, the columns that identify a row (its grain) and the notes its data contract declares:

gcd_describe("graduation_rate_4_year_cohort")
#> ── Four-Year Cohort Graduation Rate (graduation_rate_4_year_cohort) ────────────
#> Share of the four-year high school cohort that graduated, by school, district,
#> and state and demographic subgroup, 2004-2025.
#> 
#> Source: Governor's Office of Education and Workforce Strategy (GOEWS, formerly
#> GOSA)
#> Years: 2004-2025
#> Detail levels: districts, schools (default), states
#> Grain: year, district_code, school_code, demographic
#> Key metric: graduation_rate
#> Columns: 7 (see `$columns`); filters: 18 (see `$filters`)
#> 
#> ── Notes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> * Missing values: NA means suppressed (small counts), not zero; zeros are real
#>   from 2010 on.
#> * Limitations: 2004-2010 figures predate Georgia's adoption of the federal
#>   four-year adjusted-cohort methodology (ACGR, first reported 2011) and use the
#>   state's earlier leaver-based rate; the 2010->2011 state rate drop (~81% to
#>   ~67%) is a methodology break, not a real decline — do not trend across it.
#>   Suppressed cells are NULL (not zero) from 2010 onward, but 2004-2009 sources
#>   use literal ZEROS for suppressed cells — a zero rate/count in those years may
#>   be real or suppressed and cannot be distinguished; treat very small cohorts
#>   in 2004-2009 with caution. num_cohort is NULL for every row in 2012-2016 (the
#>   source publishes no denominator in those years). The 2004 file lists every
#>   public school, including elementary and middle schools with no graduating
#>   cohort, so 1,703 of its 2,037 all-students school rows have no graduate count
#>   or rate; from 2005 only schools with a graduating cohort are listed (344 in
#>   2005). School rows do not always sum to the published district row: of the
#>   42,815 district rows (all subgroups) with a published num_graduates and at
#>   least one published school value, 468 publish a district num_graduates below
#>   the sum of its school rows, 49 of them among the 4,039 all-students rows
#>   (source-published, 2005-2025; e.g. 2016 Whitfield 709 vs 810, 2014 Richmond
#>   economically_disadvantaged 582 vs 1,286) — use the official district/state
#>   rows for rollups rather than summing school rows. economically_disadvantaged
#>   is not a like-for-like group across years. Statewide it is 55-56% of the
#>   cohort in 2017-2021, then 47% (2022), 53% (2023), 61% (2024) and 66% (2025),
#>   and district coding shifts: Cobb County puts 98% of its 2021 cohort in the
#>   group (36-38% in 2017-2020 and 2023, 20% in 2022) and under 2% of its
#>   graduates in 2011, 2012 and 2014, and districts with 100+ graduates that
#>   report 10% or less of them in the group or suppress it number 6-11 a year in
#>   2021-2023 (0-2 a year in 2016-2020). GOEWS does not document these shifts.
#>   The group's graduation rate moves when its membership does, so check its
#>   share of the cohort before comparing it across years or districts. The race
#>   axis uses the combined asian_pacific_islander bucket — not comparable
#>   row-for-row with split-convention topics without aggregating those topics'
#>   asian + pacific_islander rows at query time. State rows have NULL
#>   district_code and school_code; district rows have NULL school_code.
#> * Series break in 2011: From 2011 Georgia reports the federal four-year
#>   adjusted-cohort graduation rate, while 2004-2010 use the state's earlier
#>   leaver-based count, so the state rate falls from 0.808 (2010) to 0.675 (2011)
#>   and the cohort rises from 113,364 to 131,012 because the method changed, not
#>   because fewer students graduated.

gcd_columns() is the column dictionary. For each metric it gives the unit and, for counts, whether it is a rate’s numerator or denominator:

gcd_columns("graduation_rate_4_year_cohort") |>
  select(column, type, role, unit, metric_component)
#> # A tibble: 7 × 5
#>   column          type    role           unit       metric_component
#>   <chr>           <chr>   <chr>          <chr>      <chr>           
#> 1 year            integer year           <NA>       <NA>            
#> 2 district_code   string  fk_district    <NA>       <NA>            
#> 3 school_code     string  fk_school      <NA>       <NA>            
#> 4 demographic     string  fk_demographic <NA>       <NA>            
#> 5 num_graduates   integer metric         count      numerator       
#> 6 num_cohort      integer metric         count      denominator     
#> 7 graduation_rate number  metric         proportion <NA>

Some categorical columns have no total. gcd_describe() lists them under “Pick one value of”: for example, grade_cluster and subject in ccrpi_content_mastery, whose values must not be mixed in one summary.

d <- gcd_describe("ccrpi_content_mastery")
d$filters |>
  filter(kind == "categorical") |>
  select(param, has_total, requires_single_value)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 3
#>   param           has_total requires_single_value
#>   <chr>           <lgl>     <lgl>                
#> 1 grade_cluster   FALSE     TRUE                 
#> 2 assessment_type FALSE     FALSE                
#> 3 subject         FALSE     TRUE                 
#> 4 ccrpi_flag      FALSE     FALSE

Get rows

gcd_rows() returns a tibble typed from the schema. Codes stay character (leading zeros survive), years are integers, and proportions stay on the 0-1 scale. Every place comes with its name beside its code.

By name or by code

Name a district, school or county and the package turns it into a code. Names match exactly, ignoring case, accents and a trailing “County”, and former names work too:

riverwood <- gcd_rows(
  "graduation_rate_4_year_cohort",
  district = "Fulton County",
  school = "Riverwood High School",   # a former name
  demographic = "all",
  year = 2021:2025
)
#> ℹ Demographic groups overlap across categories and may overlap within a
#>   category (active_duty can be a subset of military_connected). Read the
#>   dataset's definitions and non_additive declarations. Use the published `all`
#>   total when available, never add it to its subgroups. Counts reconcile only
#>   for complete, disjoint groups; subgroup rates generally do not add to the
#>   overall rate.
riverwood |>
  select(year, district_code, school_code, school_name, graduation_rate)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 5
#>    year district_code school_code school_name                    graduation_rate
#>   <int> <chr>         <chr>       <chr>                                    <dbl>
#> 1  2021 660           3066        Riverwood International Chart…           0.934
#> 2  2022 660           3066        Riverwood International Chart…           0.975
#> 3  2023 660           3066        Riverwood International Chart…           0.969
#> 4  2024 660           3066        Riverwood International Chart…           0.988
#> 5  2025 660           3066        Riverwood International Chart…           0.971

A name that matches more than one place stops with the candidates instead of guessing. “Eastside Elementary School” is in several districts, and Fulton County has an old and a new “Milton High School”:

gcd_rows("graduation_rate_4_year_cohort", school = "Milton High School",
         district = "Fulton County")
#> Error in `gcd_rows()`:
#> ! "Milton High School" matches more than one school.
#> ℹ Use `school_id` with one "DISTRICT-SCHOOL" code.
#> • 660-0106: Milton High School (Fulton County, active)
#> • 660-2060: Milton High School (Fulton County, inactive)

Codes work everywhere names do. A school is identified by its district and school codes together, written "DISTRICT-SCHOOL" in school_id:

gcd_rows("graduation_rate_4_year_cohort", school_id = "660-0106",
         demographic = "all", year = 2025, quiet = TRUE) |>
  select(year, school_code, school_name, num_graduates, num_cohort, graduation_rate)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>    year school_code school_name        num_graduates num_cohort graduation_rate
#>   <int> <chr>       <chr>                      <int>      <int>           <dbl>
#> 1  2025 0106        Milton High School           502        522           0.962

Years and detail levels

year = 2021:2025 asks for a range; year = c(2015, 2025) asks for those two years only. Each call returns one detail level: schools, districts, states, counties or tracts, whatever the dataset publishes. The default is the finest level (counties for Census datasets). Columns that would be empty at a level are left out:

state <- gcd_rows("graduation_rate_4_year_cohort", detail = "states",
                  demographic = "all", year = c(2015, 2025), quiet = TRUE)
state
#> # A tibble: 2 × 7
#>    year demographic demographic_label demographic_category num_graduates
#>   <int> <chr>       <chr>             <chr>                        <int>
#> 1  2015 all         All               aggregate                    98465
#> 2  2025 all         All               aggregate                   123911
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: num_cohort <int>, graduation_rate <dbl>

To combine levels, call once per level and bind the rows.

What NA means

A missing metric usually means the value was suppressed to protect privacy (small counts), not zero. The schema’s null_semantics says which, and gcd_rows() prints the API’s advisory when a result holds suppressed values:

small <- gcd_rows("graduation_rate_4_year_cohort", district = "Appling County",
                  year = 2024, detail = "districts")
#> ℹ This result contains NULL metric cells, which mean the value was SUPPRESSED
#>   (small counts), not zero — do not report or chart a NULL as 0 (see
#>   null_semantics and each column's null_meaning).
#> ℹ Demographic groups overlap across categories and may overlap within a
#>   category (active_duty can be a subset of military_connected). Read the
#>   dataset's definitions and non_additive declarations. Use the published `all`
#>   total when available, never add it to its subgroups. Counts reconcile only
#>   for complete, disjoint groups; subgroup rates generally do not add to the
#>   overall rate.
#> ℹ `district_census_id` is a 5-digit Census school-district code, NOT a county
#>   FIPS, and a district is not 1:1 with a county — do not map these district
#>   rows as counties.
small |>
  select(demographic, num_graduates, num_cohort, graduation_rate)
#> # A tibble: 18 × 4
#>    demographic                    num_graduates num_cohort graduation_rate
#>    <chr>                                  <int>      <int>           <dbl>
#>  1 active_duty                               NA         NA          NA    
#>  2 all                                      225        240           0.938
#>  3 asian_pacific_islander                    NA         NA          NA    
#>  4 black                                     57         62           0.919
#>  5 economically_disadvantaged               225        240           0.938
#>  6 english_learners                          13         14           0.929
#>  7 female                                   111        114           0.974
#>  8 foster_care                               NA         NA          NA    
#>  9 hispanic                                  42         44           0.954
#> 10 homeless                                  NA         NA          NA    
#> 11 male                                     114        126           0.905
#> 12 migrant                                   18         20           0.9  
#> 13 multiracial                               NA         NA          NA    
#> 14 native_american                           NA         NA          NA    
#> 15 not_economically_disadvantaged            NA         NA          NA    
#> 16 students_with_disabilities                25         31           0.807
#> 17 students_without_disabilities            200        209           0.957
#> 18 white                                    119        127           0.937

The advisories stay with the result in gcd_meta(small)$advisories; quiet = TRUE (or options(gcd.quiet = TRUE)) silences the messages.

Totals beside subgroups

Nothing is pinned by default, so a result holds the all total beside every subgroup, and subgroups from different categories overlap (a student is in a race group, a gender group and an economic group at once). Never add them up:

fulton <- gcd_rows("graduation_rate_4_year_cohort", district = "Fulton County",
                   detail = "districts", year = 2025, quiet = TRUE)

fulton |>
  summarise(
    published_total = num_cohort[demographic == "all"],
    sum_of_every_row = sum(num_cohort, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   published_total sum_of_every_row
#>             <int>            <int>
#> 1            7934            39902

Use the published all row for totals, and filter one category (demographic_category = "race") to compare groups.

Which values exist: gcd_values()

When a filter returns nothing, gcd_values() shows which combinations exist under the other filters, with row counts, without downloading rows:

gcd_values("ccrpi_content_mastery", c("grade_cluster", "subject"),
           year = 2025, detail = "districts")
#> # A tibble: 11 × 3
#>    grade_cluster subject               n_rows
#>    <chr>         <chr>                  <int>
#>  1 elementary    english_language_arts   2340
#>  2 elementary    mathematics             2340
#>  3 elementary    science                 2340
#>  4 high          english_language_arts   2340
#>  5 high          mathematics             2340
#>  6 high          science                 2340
#>  7 high          social_studies          2340
#>  8 middle        english_language_arts   2340
#>  9 middle        mathematics             2340
#> 10 middle        science                 2340
#> 11 middle        social_studies          2340

Lookup tables

The six lookup tables (districts, schools, counties, tracts, block_groups, demographics) hold more than names: school addresses, coordinates, grade spans, locale and charter status, tract populations. gcd_dimension() returns them:

schools <- gcd_dimension("schools",
                         columns = c("district_code", "school_code", "locale"))
schools
#> # A tibble: 4,372 × 3
#>    district_code school_code locale
#>    <chr>         <chr>       <chr> 
#>  1 601           0103        town  
#>  2 601           0109        rural 
#>  3 601           0177        town  
#>  4 601           0195        rural 
#>  5 601           0277        <NA>  
#>  6 601           1050        rural 
#>  7 601           2050        <NA>  
#>  8 601           5050        rural 
#>  9 601           6412        <NA>  
#> 10 601           6701        town  
#> # ℹ 4,362 more rows

School codes repeat across districts, so always join on both codes:

schools |> count(school_code, sort = TRUE) |> head(3)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>   school_code     n
#>   <chr>       <int>
#> 1 8010          198
#> 2 8012          175
#> 3 8013          166

high_schools <- gcd_rows("graduation_rate_4_year_cohort", detail = "schools",
                         demographic = "all", year = 2025, quiet = TRUE) |>
  left_join(schools, by = c("district_code", "school_code"))

high_schools |>
  filter(!is.na(locale)) |>
  group_by(locale) |>
  summarise(schools = n(),
            graduation_rate = sum(num_graduates, na.rm = TRUE) /
              sum(num_cohort[!is.na(num_graduates)], na.rm = TRUE))
#> # A tibble: 4 × 3
#>   locale schools graduation_rate
#>   <chr>    <int>           <dbl>
#> 1 city        95           0.874
#> 2 rural      183           0.905
#> 3 suburb     174           0.877
#> 4 town        70           0.932

That last step pools the rate from its counts. Averaging rates (mean(graduation_rate)) would weigh a school of 40 like a school of 2,000.

Cite the data

The data is CC BY 4.0. gcd_citation() writes the credit, from a result or a dataset name:

gcd_citation(riverwood)
#> [1] "Four-Year Cohort Graduation Rate. Georgia Civic Data (georgiacivicdata.org), CC BY 4.0. https://georgiacivicdata.org/api/v1/datasets/graduation_rate_4_year_cohort. Original source: Governor's Office of Education and Workforce Strategy (GOEWS, formerly GOSA)."

Caching

Metadata (the catalog, schemas and lookup tables) is cached for the R session. Rows can also be cached on disk, if you ask:

options(gcd.cache = TRUE)   # or cache = TRUE in gcd_rows()

Cached responses are kept with their ETag in tools::R_user_dir("georgiacivicdata", "cache"), and each repeat asks the server whether the data changed: an unchanged answer reuses the saved copy without downloading, and a new data release downloads afresh (a response the server marks fresh, for five minutes, is reused without asking). gcd_cache_clear() empties both caches.
